_readme: QUALITATIVE per-chain dossier — the intelligence that filings and store counts do NOT carry:
a chain's HISTORY, its most POPULAR ITEMS, its FLAGSHIP / best-known OUTLETS, and loose NOTES.
A Pro-tier dimension that sits beside the measured numbers (store counts, financial_anchors,
opening pace). PRO ONLY — never written to the public map/data.
PROVENANCE, same posture as the rest of the project. Every item carries `as_of` + `source`
(a `source_url` where there is one) and a `confidence`: 'high' for a primary filing / company
statement, 'medium' for reputable press, 'low' for a single weak mention. NEVER fabricate; an
unknown field is simply absent. First-party / official / filings / reputable press / licensed
sources only — NO review/delivery/aggregator platforms (Dianping, Meituan, 窄门餐眼, …).
SHAPE. brands[<chain_id>] may hold any of:
popular_items   [ {name, note?, as_of, source, source_url?, confidence}, … ]
flagship_outlets[ {name, city?, note?, as_of, source, source_url?, confidence}, … ]
Measured figures (avg store area, orders/day, AUV, store counts) do NOT live here — they go to
the `financial_anchors` table (measured) and `china_stores.json` (counts). This file is prose.

history.text: Founded 1997 in Zhengzhou, Henan by Zhang Hongchao (张红超) as a cold-drinks and shaved-ice stand; grew into an ultra-low-price bubble-tea and soft-serve franchise and by 2025 was the world's largest F&B chain by store count. Listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (2097.HK) in March 2025.
history.source: Mixue Group HKEX listing / global offering prospectus (2097.HK, 2025)

popular_items.name: Fresh ice cream cone (冰淇淋)
popular_items.note: The brand's best-known draw — a ~¥2-4 soft-serve cone.
popular_items.source: Mixue prospectus product mix and reputable press

popular_items.name: Lemonade (柠檬水)
popular_items.note: ~¥4 fresh lemonade, a flagship high-volume SKU.

notes.text: The 'Snow King' (雪王) mascot is central to the brand's marketing and recognition.

history.text: Auntea Jenny (沪上阿姨, 'Shanghai Auntie') is a Shanghai mid-priced freshly-made tea chain founded in 2013, known for grain-forward '五谷' milk teas and fruit teas. It franchises aggressively — ~9,000+ stores, overwhelmingly franchised — and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (2589.HK) in December 2024, after which it accelerated an overseas push (Malaysia first, then Australia, the UK, South Korea and Indonesia).
history.source: Auntea Jenny IPO prospectus / HKEX listing (2589.HK, Dec 2024)

popular_items.name: Grain milk tea (五谷/杂粮奶茶)
popular_items.note: The brand's signature grain-forward milk tea — its best-known positioning.
popular_items.source: Auntea Jenny brand positioning / reputable press

popular_items.name: Royal Fruit Tea (XL)
popular_items.note: A viral oversized fruit tea (watermelon/orange/mango/lemon) reported at the Seoul launch; served with a spork to eat the fruit.
popular_items.source: Korean food blog (chingumobile free board), weak single source

notes.text: Trades under its Chinese identity 沪上阿姨 ('Shanghai Auntie') across its overseas markets; romanized 'Hu Shang Ayi'.

history.text: Founded 2010 in Beijing by Wang Ning as a general variety/trinket shop; pivoted toward designer-toy blind boxes around 2014-2016, with the 2016 Molly blind-box collaboration (artist Kenny Wong) marking the turn into IP-driven collectibles. Listed on HKEX in Dec 2020 (9992.HK).
history.source: company-history press profiles (brandwiki, NBC/Forbes coverage of Wang Ning)

popular_items.name: LABUBU (The Monsters series)
popular_items.note: the chain's global breakout IP; press reporting on FY2024 results tied ~US$423M of group revenue to Labubu dolls, +729% YoY

notes.text: Founder/chairman/CEO Wang Ning holds ~48.7% of the company; Forbes put his net worth at ~US$22.7bn in June 2025, China's 10th richest person at the time.

history.text: Founded Oct 2017 (Beijing, later headquartered Xiamen) by Qian Zhiya (Jenny Qian) and Lu Zhengyao (Charles Lu); built on a mobile-order, cashier-light kiosk model to undercut Starbucks on price. A 2020 accounting scandal (then-COO Jian Liu found to have fabricated ~RMB2.2bn/US$314M in 2019 sales) led to a Nasdaq delisting; the company rebuilt and in June 2023 overtook Starbucks by store count in China.

popular_items.name: Coconut Latte (椰云拿铁)
popular_items.note: flagship hit drink; press reporting described peak sales near 2 million cups/day

popular_items.name: Brown Sugar Boba Latte / Cheese Latte

history.text: Founded 1994 in Jianyang, Sichuan, by Zhang Yong (with Shi Yonghong, Shu Ping and Li Haiyan); grew from a four-table storefront into one of the world's largest hot pot chains, known for highly attentive, theatrical tableside service. First overseas restaurant opened at Clarke Quay, Singapore, in 2012; North America operations now run through the separately listed Super Hi International (HKEX 9658 / Nasdaq HDL).

popular_items.name: Sichuan-style hot pot broths (mala spicy + milder options)
Tableside hand-pulled noodle dance
popular_items.note: signature service theater (not a dish), the chain's best-known table-side ritual

history.text: Founded Nov 2017 in Kunming, Yunnan, by Zhang Junjie, who trained at a local tea-shop chain (Dawei Milk Tea) from 2010; the Chinese name 霸王茶姬 references the opera Farewell My Concubine. Headquarters later moved toward Chengdu (dual-HQ setup, with overseas operations managed from Shanghai). Listed on Nasdaq (CHA) via a 2025 20-F.

popular_items.name: Jasmine Green Milk Tea / Boya Juexian (伯牙绝弦)
popular_items.note: the chain's signature no-boba, tea-forward bestseller; company states over 100 million cups sold per year

history.text: Company 北京乐自天成 registered 2012-07-09 (legal rep / CEO Chen Wei 陈威); the 52TOYS brand launched 2015, co-led by Chen Wei and Huang Jin (黄今, 三国杀/Yoka co-founder). A full-chain IP-toy company (incubation, design, production, omni-channel) on an 'own IP + licensed IP' dual-drive — per its 22 May 2025 HKEX A1, 35 owned IPs (incl. 猛兽匣 Beastbox, 胖哒幼 Panda Roll) + 80 licensed (incl. Crayon Shin-chan, Tom & Jerry), ~2,800 SKUs. 3rd-largest IP-toy company by 2024 China GMV (claims #2 in the multi-category niche). The A1 (sponsors Citi + Huatai) LAPSED on 22 Nov 2025.

popular_items.name: 猛兽匣 Beastbox
popular_items.note: 52TOYS's signature own IP — transforming mecha/beast figures

popular_items.name: Licensed lines: Crayon Shin-chan 蜡笔小新, Tom & Jerry 猫和老鼠

notes.text: The A1 quantifies the channel-led thesis: ~2/3 of revenue runs through dealers (66.8% in 2024) vs ~31% self-operated, even as own China stores shrank 19->5 and revenue grew RMB463M->630M (2022-24). But it is LOSS-MAKING and the loss WIDENED (RMB1.7M->71.9M->122M), and licensed-IP revenue share rose to 64.5% (2024) while own-IP fell to 24.5% = rising license-concentration. Overseas revenue CAGR >100%. Losses are the likely reason the A1 lapsed 22 Nov 2025 without listing.

history.text: BON APPéTIT (branded BA / BA烘焙; the name is the French mealtime blessing 'bon appétit') is a French-technique artisan bakery created in Kunming, Yunnan, around the concept 'le pain est vivant' — 'bread is alive.' Its house philosophy is 真/鲜/制: natural ingredients, hand-made fresh in-store with no frozen dough, and slow natural ('wild') fermentation. BA frames itself as 'a company that came out of the mountains,' fusing French baking with Eastern-highland Yunnan terroir — Himalayan rose salt, wild black truffle, and mountain spring water — and adapts its method to altitude (far less yeast at Shangri-La's ~3,200 m) and Yunnan's dry climate.
history.source: BON APPéTIT (BA) founder interview — Zhihu (面包王子)

popular_items.name: Black Truffle series (黑松露系列)
popular_items.note: Black Truffle Baguette, Sashimi Black Truffle Baguette, Black Truffle Croissant — using fresh Yunnan/Shangri-La black truffle (BA notes ~1/3 of the world's black truffle comes from Yunnan).
popular_items.source: BON APPéTIT (BA) founder interview — Zhihu (面包王子)

popular_items.name: BABAguette series
popular_items.note: Yunnan ingredients in baguettes — 老奶洋芋 (mashed-potato) and 滇式卤鸡 (Yunnan braised-chicken); a pun on French 'baguette' and the Yunnan word for staple food, 'BABA'.
popular_items.source: BON APPéTIT (BA) founder interview — Zhihu (面包王子)

popular_items.name: 山地鲜包包 mountain fresh-buns
popular_items.note: 墨江紫米乳酪 (Mojiang purple-rice cheese) and 斑马流沙蛋黄 (zebra salted lava egg-yolk).
popular_items.source: BON APPéTIT (BA) founder interview — Zhihu (面包王子)

flagship_outlets.name: BA1903
flagship_outlets.note: Themed on the Yunnan-Vietnam (meter-gauge) Railway heritage (1903/1910), which first brought French coffee-and-crusty-bread culture to Kunming.
flagship_outlets.source: BON APPéTIT (BA) founder interview — Zhihu (面包王子)

flagship_outlets.name: Songtsam Shangri-La (松赞香格里拉店)
flagship_outlets.note: A '3,300 m-altitude artisan bakery' inside a Songtsam hotel, using local mountain spring water; positioned as a world-class high-altitude artisan store.
flagship_outlets.source: BON APPéTIT (BA) founder interview — Zhihu (面包王子)

flagship_outlets.name: Bellevue (North America flagship)
flagship_outlets.note: 550 106th Ave NE Ste 102 (Bellevue Connection); opened Jan 2026; BA's stated North America flagship per babakery.com.

flagship_outlets.name: Dubai Artisan Theme Store
flagship_outlets.note: BA's Dubai store, listed as an 'Artisan Theme Store' on the brand site; its first Gulf location.

notes.text: Chongqing has reportedly been a standout market — per the founder, per-store performance there outpaces home-base Kunming despite local taste differences, on identical products — a sign the Yunnan-terroir concept travels beyond its region.
notes.source: BON APPéTIT (BA) founder interview — Zhihu (面包王子)

notes.text: Technique as identity: altitude and dry climate force recipe adaptation (sharply reduced yeast, Napoleon flour as a base, tangzhong 烫种 + levain 鲁邦种), which BA presents as a distinct Southwest-China / Yunnan baker identity rather than a copy of French or Japanese bread.
notes.source: BON APPéTIT (BA) founder interview — Zhihu (面包王子)
